name: Thanos / Grafana Mimir
model: Prometheus metrics with PromQL, made global and long-term: one query view over many Prometheus servers and tenants, years of retention
engine_note: Prometheus TSDB blocks (immutable, two-hour, then compacted) kept in object storage (S3, GCS, Azure); store gateways and caches serve queries
consistency: No transactions. Mimir replicates each series to 3 ingesters by default (or Kafka in ingest-storage mode) before ack; Thanos sidecar uploads blocks after Prometheus cuts them, so the newest ~2 h live only on Prometheus.
scaling: Horizontal, microservices: stateless queriers, sharded ingesters (Mimir, Thanos Receive), compactors and store gateways; object storage holds all history.
licence: Thanos: Apache License 2.0; Grafana Mimir: AGPLv3

licence_events.event: Grafana Labs launches Mimir as an AGPLv3 fork of Cortex (Apache 2.0), including features that were previously commercial

reach: Reach for one when you run many Prometheus servers or clusters and need a single query view, multi-tenancy and months to years of metrics on object storage.
avoid: Avoid for a single cluster with weeks of retention: plain Prometheus is simpler; both add many components to run.
escape: One Prometheus cannot hold years of metrics from many clusters; these put Prometheus blocks on object storage.
chat: Global, long-retention metrics across all regions serving the chat product, for capacity planning.
notes: CLAIM CHECK (e) 'Thanos, Mimir and Cortex ship Prometheus's immutable blocks into object storage': VERIFIED FOR THANOS SIDECAR, CORRECTED FOR MIMIR AND CORTEX. Thanos design doc (https://thanos.io/tip/thanos/design.md/): 'The storage engine periodically produces immutable blocks of data for a fixed time range.' 'Those block files can be backed up to object storage and later be queried by another component' and 'All data is uploaded as it is created by the Prometheus server/storage engine.' So Thanos (sidecar mode) ships Prometheus's own blocks. Mimir and Cortex do not take Prometheus's blocks: Prometheus sends samples by remote write, and their own ingesters build Prometheus-format TSDB blocks and upload those. Mimir ingester doc: 'In-memory series are periodically compacted into an on-disk format called a TSDB block and then uploaded to object storage. This process happens every two hours by default.' Cortex blocks storage doc (https://cortexmetrics.io/docs/blocks-storage/): 'a Cortex storage engine based on Prometheus TSDB: it stores each tenant's time series into their own TSDB which write out their series to a on-disk block (defaults to 2h block range periods)'. Suggested wording: 'Thanos uploads Prometheus's own blocks; Mimir and Cortex receive samples by remote write and write the same block format to object storage.' (Thanos Receive works like Mimir.) Mimir replication quote: 'writing each series to RF different ingesters, where RF is the replication factor, three, by default'; Mimir ingest storage: 'distributors shard incoming series across Kafka partitions'. Mimir announcement: fetch tool reported publication 2022-03-31; URL path says 2022/03/30 (time zone difference). Licences checked from raw LICENSE files: Mimir AGPLv3, Thanos Apache 2.0. licence_class copyleft reflects Mimir; Thanos is permissive. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is Cortex-based per AWS (not re-verified), so not listed. No Jepsen analysis.
